title: Tell HN: Notion AI chat sessions have been exposed via Fireworks AI hack
summary:
Only an email so far, nothing official I could find. I figure if you didn't get this email you are ok.

---

We are writing to inform you of a security incident at one of our vendors, Fireworks AI, that may impact you. For the latest on the Fireworks AI incident, see their official updates here.

Following an investigation by the Notion security team, we have determined that your workspace, [...], was among the <1% of Notion workspaces that may have been affected by the Fireworks security incident. Some unattributable chat sessions with Notion AI may have been exposed in this incident. “Unattributable” means the chats weren't labeled with who wrote them or which workspace they came from, and the transcripts did not contain tool call results. Beyond what’s in the chat transcript itself, there’s no information tying the chat back to your workspace, users, or company. No other data from within your workspace is affected.

This email explains what happened, what data of yours might be affected, what we’re doing to address this, and what we recommend to protect your data from this Fireworks AI incident.

What is Fireworks AI and how we used them: Fireworks is one of the most used global AI infrastructure platforms powering tens of thousands of customers and used by hundreds of thousands of developers. We used Fireworks for classification jobs to help customers understand their own AI usage through a feature in Notion called Insights, and we used them as a general inference provider to serve open-weight models inside our product. The Insights feature has been disabled as we investigate this incident, and we are no longer serving open-weight models through Fireworks.

What happened and how we addressed it: We learned from Fireworks about potential incidents earlier this month, and we shut down all connections to their systems out of an abundance of caution.

On November 6, Fireworks notified us that malicious actors may have accessed potential customer data. Our team immediately began another internal investigation. On November 8, Fireworks confirmed this new dataset for us.

Upon analysis of the new data, we discovered that it included unattributable Notion AI chat transcripts used for the Insights feature. Chats weren't labeled with who wrote them or which workspace they came from, and the transcripts did not contain any tool call results. Beyond the words in the chat transcripts themselves, the data contained no information that could specifically identify your workspace, users, or company.

No other Notion data from your workspace is affected, and we continue to monitor this incident.

Recommended next steps for you: You can retrieve and review the impacted data securely inside your workspace. See below:

- [...]

We recommend that you treat this data as if it were exposed. If anyone on your team might have pasted sensitive information into chats in Notion AI like passwords, API keys, or other credentials during this timeframe, please rotate them now.

You trust us with your life's work in Notion, and that trust covers every partner we choose. In this critical time for global security, it is our mission to raise the standard for how your data is protected. You have our uncompromising commitment.

---

I downloaded the dataset and it's a full chat for me.

title: OpenAI models have no agency anymore
summary:
I don't know if it's a token saving measure or to bait more interactivity from users but it feels like out of nowhere the models have just became useless with zero agency. If you don't have a goal plugin that constantly prods them, there is a very high chance it just doesn't do anything and responds back like you're asking it a question.

OFTEN it ends sentences with "I'll do XXXXX." or "I'll implement XXXXX." and STOPS where the next turn should be a tool call or something. Because of this I genuinely thought it was a Pi or opencodex regression stopping the turn right before an expected tool call. But no, it's because the models are incredibly lazy now.

This came out of nowhere.

title: Playwright Stud – Record and run Playwright tests directly
summary:
Hi HN,

I built Playwright Stud because configuring Node.js, setting up CLIs, and managing locators just to run quick smoke tests or generate clean scripts can slow down a team's momentum—especially for QA engineers migrating to automation.

It is a 219 KiB extension that packages a test recorder, an in-browser runner with live visual step highlighting, a network mock builder, an auth state exporter, and a multi-layered site auditor.

Key technical aspects: - 100% Privacy-First: No third-party servers, tracking, or cloud databases. Everything runs locally inside your browser tab and saves to chrome.storage.local. It is safe for corporate/internal staging environments. - Smart Locators: The recorder automatically favors accessibility-first semantic locators (getByRole, getByLabel, getByTestId) rather than brittle, generated absolute XPaths. - Self-Healing Tab Execution: When UI variations occur during a live in-browser run, the script fallback engine automatically tests up to 8 alternative element strategies in real-time.

I would love to get your feedback on the execution flow, developer ergonomics, or any features you would like to see added next!

https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/playwright-stud/eodfkbagoeghobkkfpcfpacnnpgidhhd?authuser=0&hl=en

title: Tell HN: Some of My Recent Ideas
summary:
I thought it'll be fun to share some different ideas that I've had AI build in the last couple of weeks or months. Using my local Qwen 27b model.

I had AI build a Roku remote in the web and connect to my jelly fin so I can easily search for shows and autoplay them on my Roku. Also features an API and I can scan an NFC tag and it will automatically open a video on my Roku.

I have an HD home run so I had AI build me a DVR page, it could use some work but overall it's working and it's pretty cool.

I've been building a health ecosystem tracking food journaling about health, and then adding NFC tags to different medications and supplements. I had to build a Android app that sinks any of my NFC tag scans automatically to my server. Since I don't run tailscale or anything like that to get in and out of my network.

I have a game boy color cartridge with SD card. I thought it would be fun to add ebooks. Haven't tested this one yet but in theory I'll be able to copy books onto my game boy color cartridge and then use my game boy Pocket to read books lol.

I have a Ricoh theta S, that used to have an app, but doesn't appear to work with latest Ricoh apps lately. So it's building me an app so I can take 360 photos, and embed gps, and time/date info easily. (Basically connect to my phone so it happens automatically).

I have a handful more but I'll stop there for now.

Got any fun ideas you've been playing with?

(I'm not building any of these for money, they are for my own personal enjoyment).

I might post a spec/prompt to my blog for these at some point but for now this is all you get.
